response.rationale: Rapid onset of visual loss, diabetes insipidus, and central hypothyroidism with a homogeneously enhancing sellar/suprasellar mass and a previously normal pituitary strongly favor lymphocytic hypophysitis. Pituitary adenoma is common but rarely causes DI; craniopharyngioma and meningioma fit less well with the imaging and clinical pattern.

rejected.why: Pituitary adenoma is a common sellar mass but diabetes insipidus is atypical, and the rapid clinical course with homogeneous enhancement is more consistent with hypophysitis.
Craniopharyngioma can cause visual loss and DI but typically appears cystic/calcified and heterogeneous, not as a diffusely homogeneously enhancing mass.
Meningioma can enhance homogeneously but less commonly causes DI and acute hypopituitarism; the T2 hyperintensity and sellar involvement with posterior pituitary symptoms favor hypophysitis.
